usage: malac-hd [-h] -m MAPPING [-co CONVERT_OUTPUT]
                [-l {python,javascript,java,csharp}] [-ti TRANSFORM_INPUT]
                [-to TRANSFORM_OUTPUT] [-mod MODELS [MODELS ...]]
                [-sr SUPPORTING_RESOURCE [SUPPORTING_RESOURCE ...]] [-min]
                [-s]

You are using the MApping LAnguage Compiler for Health Data, short MaLaC-HD.
We differentiate between two modes, CONVERTING and TRANSFORMING.
The CONVERSION is done by compiling a given mapping to Python (default), JavaScript, Java or C# code, that itself can be run with its own argument handling for TRANSFORMING input files.
Additionally, the TRANSFORMATION can also be be done by MaLaC-HD directly after CONVERSION, i.e. for direct testing purposes.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -m, --mapping MAPPING
                        the mapping file path, the conversion/mapping rule language is detected by file ending, right now FML maps (*.map), FHIR R4 (*.4.fhir.xml) StructureMaps and ConceptMaps can be given as mappings
  -co, --convert_output CONVERT_OUTPUT
                        the conversion output file path (a .py, .js, .java or .cs file, depending on --language), if not given, saved in the working directory with the map-file name.
                        A Java or C# class is named like its file, so the name of a .java or .cs file has to be one such a class can have
                        (and no reserved word). A .jar (with --language java) or .dll (with --language csharp) file gets the class compiled
                        with the JDK or the .NET SDK instead: a program, which runs with `java -jar Mapping.jar` or `dotnet Mapping.dll` and
                        takes the same options as a Python script, with the jars or assemblies of malac-utils and of the models it uses next
                        to it (those MALAC_HD_JAVA_JARS or MALAC_HD_DOTNET_ASSEMBLIES names: `python -m malac.hd.runtime.java` or `.dotnet
